record.original_question: For the binary digit-reversal permutation that sends an integer with binary expansion 1a_1…a_ℓ to the integer with expansion 1a_ℓ…a_1, explain why the associated 4-regular graphs resemble several small manifolds connected by a line, and make that visual structure mathematically precise.

evidence.quote: This sequence (A059893) is a simple permutation of the integers: if n has expansion 1a_1 . . . a_ℓ in base 2, then a_n is given by the integer 1a_ℓ . . . a_1.
One would perhaps also expect that it is somehow connected to the van der Corput sequence and it does, visually, look somewhat similar: we see several small manifolds that are connected via a line.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a permutation σ on the positive integers as follows. For n ≥ 1, write n in binary as n = 1 a_1 a_2 … a_ℓ (with leading bit 1), and set σ(n) to be the integer with binary expansion 1 a_ℓ a_{ℓ-1} … a_1. (Equivalently, σ is the sequence OEIS A059893.)

For each integer N ≥ 1, build a 4-regular graph G_N on the vertex set {1, 2, …, N} by joining, for every n ∈ {1, …, N}, the vertex n to the vertices n-1, n+1, σ(n)-1, σ(n)+1 (whenever these lie in {1, …, N}, and discarding loops and multiple edges). Embed G_N in the plane by placing vertex n at position (n, σ(n)/n) (or any other natural embedding that reflects the values of σ).

Numerical plots of G_N for large N display a sequence of localized "clumps" connected to one another by an essentially one-dimensional path.

Problem. Make this observation precise. Specifically:
(a) Identify and rigorously describe the clumps: give a sequence of index intervals I_k ⊂ ℕ on which the induced subgraphs G_N[I_k] form a family of dense connected "manifold-like" pieces (for instance, by exhibiting the asymptotic geometry, diameter, and edge density of these subgraphs as k → ∞).
(b) Show that, after suitable normalization, the connecting structure between consecutive clumps consists of a uniformly bounded-width strip (a "line"), and quantify its width in terms of N.
(c) Relate this decomposition to the dyadic block structure n ∈ [2^k, 2^{k+1}) on which σ acts as bit-reversal of length k, and to the van der Corput sequence φ_2(n) = ∑ a_i 2^{-i}, thereby explaining the visual similarity with the graph associated to the van der Corput sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the source preprint (arXiv:2012.04625, v2 from 2021) where this visual structure is described informally but not proved. No follow-up paper rigorously establishing the clump-and-line decomposition for the bit-reversal permutation graph was found. A 2025 preprint (arXiv:2511.00311) studies a related limiting object (Chamanara surface) for the van der Corput graph but does not address the precise structural question posed here. The status therefore appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2012.04625v2
status_evidence.snippet: Informal observation that the bit-reversal graph 'visually looks somewhat similar' to the van der Corput graph, exhibiting 'several small manifolds connected via a line,' but no rigorous statement is given.
status_evidence.claim: The visual structure is only described informally in the source preprint.

status_evidence.title: Obtaining the Chamanara Surface from the van der Corput sequence
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a limiting geometric object for the van der Corput graph; does not address the bit-reversal A059893 graph structure described above.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not resolve the bit-reversal graph decomposition question.
